text:
Predicates:
EatsSalad(x) ::: x eats salads regularly.
Conscious(x) ::: x is very conscious about their health and eating habits.
GrewUpHealthyHome(x) ::: x grew up in a health-conscious childhood home.
FulfillsNutrition(x) ::: x fulfills their nutritional daily intakes.
HasGoodRelationship(x, y) ::: x has a good relationship with y, where y are the parents.
VisitsGym(x) ::: x visits the gym at least once a day.
Taylor ::: the individual named Taylor.
Parents(x) ::: x's parents.

Premises:
∀x (GrewUpHealthyHome(x) → EatsSalad(x)) ::: All people who grew up in health-conscious homes eat salads regularly.
∀x (GrewUpHealthyHome(x) → FulfillsNutrition(x)) ::: All people who grew up in health-conscious homes fulfill their nutritional daily intakes.
∀x (HasGoodRelationship(x, y) → FulfillsNutrition(x)) ::: If people have good relationships with their parents, then they fulfill their nutritional daily intakes.
∀x (HasGoodRelationship(x, y) → ¬EatsSalad(x)) ::: If people have good relationships with their parents, then they do not eat salads regularly.
∀x (VisitsGym(x) → FulfillsNutrition(x)) ::: If people visit the gym at least once a day, then they fulfill their daily nutritional intakes.
( (GrewUpHealthyHome(Taylor) ∧ HasGoodRelationship(Taylor, Parents)) ∨ ¬(GrewUpHealthyHome(Taylor) ∨ HasGoodRelationship(Taylor, Parents)) ) ::: It is either both true that Taylor grew up in a health-conscious home and has a good relationship with her parents, or neither is true.

Conclusion:
EatsSalad(Taylor) ::: Taylor eats salads regularly.
